findings.explanation: Small behaviour change: a fly move now adds a "Fly Speed" note, so its log line reads "(Fly Speed; costs N ft)" where it used to have no parenthetical. The change is harmless and matches climb and swim, but it is not a pure refactor.

`walk_fallback` controls two things at once: whether the move can fall back to walking, and whether the check reads base speeds (`c.speeds`) or effective speed (`c.speed()`). The no-fallback refusal also hard-codes rule="GLOSS.fly-speed#1" while its message is generic. Both are fine while fly is the only no-fallback mode, so this does not block approval.

review.summary: I'm approving this fix for T-7. The per-mode table matches the old logic for walk, crawl, climb, swim, fly and unknown modes. The Speed used is the same in each case. Climbing or swimming without the Speed still costs 1 extra foot per foot (2 in Difficult Terrain) and still cancels the separate Difficult Terrain charge. Flying with no Fly Speed is still refused. A Fly Speed reduced to 0 still gets the grappled Speed 0 refusal (rule GLOSS.grappled#1, ruling R-07). The new unit tests check real costs, log notes and refusal rules against the real engine, including the edge cases of a Speed reduced to 0 and a grappled flyer. One side effect: fly moves now log a "Fly Speed" note, so they are not quite a pure refactor. One table field, `walk_fallback`, also decides which speed lookup is used. Neither is enough to reject.
